title: Etale localization and right exact transitivity of universal conormals
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $Z\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}X$ formally unramified morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use universal first-order thickenings and their quasi-coherent conormal modules as in [lem-sfb-space-universal-conormal]. The composite $vu$ is formally unramified. There is a canonical map $W_{vu}\to W_v$ extending $u$, and $Y\times_{W_v}W_{vu}$ is the universal first-order thickening of $Z$ over $Y$. Its ideal maps give a right exact sequence
$$u^*\mathcal C_{Y/X}\xrightarrow{\lambda}\mathcal C_{Z/X}\xrightarrow{\rho}\mathcal C_{Z/Y}\longrightarrow0.$$
Here tensor pullback is [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. For any commutative square $V\to U$ over a formally unramified map $B\to A$, whose vertical maps $V\to B$ and $U\to A$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], $V\to U$ is formally unramified, $W_{V/U}\to W_{B/A}$ is etale, and the induced conormal map identifies $\mathcal C_{V/U}$ with the restriction of $\mathcal C_{B/A}$ to $V$. In particular, if $B\hookrightarrow W_{B/A}$ is universal and $D\to W_{B/A}$ is etale, then $B_D=B\times_{W_{B/A}}D\hookrightarrow D$ is the universal first-order thickening of $B_D$ over $A$. These identifications are functorial in squares and identify the maps $\lambda,\rho$ above with the corresponding maps on any compatible etale charts of the tower, including charts with the identity on $X$.

source.place: Tags 060D (lemma-universal-thickening-localize), 0605 (lemma-etale-morphism-of-universal-thickenings), part (1), 060A (lemma-universal-thickening-functorial), and 06BF (lemma-transitivity-conormal-unramified); composition follows directly from the square-zero uniqueness test.

proof.text: Composition and canonical maps. For two $X$-maps $a,b:T'\to Z$ agreeing on a square-zero closed subscheme $T$, formal unramifiedness of $v$ gives $ua=ub$, and that of $u$ then gives $a=b$. Thus $vu$ is formally unramified, so its universal thickening exists by [lem-sfb-space-universal-conormal]. More generally, for a square $B\to A$ over $B_0\to A_0$ with both horizontal maps formally unramified, regard $B\hookrightarrow W_{B/A}$ as a test thickening over $A_0$. The universal property of $W_{B_0/A_0}$ gives its unique map extending $B\to B_0$. Identity and composition of these maps follow from the same uniqueness. In the tower this gives $h:W_{vu}\to W_v$. Its map on ideals gives $\lambda$: [lem-sfb-space-stalk-ideal-pullback] specifies this canonical map, rather than an arbitrary morphism of conormal modules.

source.place: Tag 060A, lemma-universal-thickening-functorial; Tag 06BF, lemma-transitivity-conormal-unramified, construction of h. Composition is the defining square-zero uniqueness test.

proof.text: The intermediate thickening. Form $P=Y\times_{W_v}W_{vu}$ using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal K$ be the ideals of $Y\hookrightarrow W_v$ and $Z\hookrightarrow W_{vu}$. The closed-subspace correspondence [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence] identifies $P\subset W_{vu}$ with the ideal $\mathcal L=\operatorname{im}(h^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_{W_{vu}})\subseteq\mathcal K$. Hence $Z\hookrightarrow P$ has ideal $\mathcal K/\mathcal L$, with square zero. Given $T\hookrightarrow T'$ over $Y$ and $T\to Z$, the universal property of $W_{vu}$ gives a unique $b:T'\to W_{vu}$ over $X$. The two maps $hb$ and $T'\to Y\hookrightarrow W_v$ are equal: they are extensions over $X$ of the same $T\to Y$, so uniqueness for $W_v$ applies. Thus $b$ factors uniquely through $P$, proving its universal property over $Y$. Uniqueness of universal thickenings identifies $P$ with $W_u$ and its ideal with $\mathcal C_{Z/Y}$; [lem-sfb-space-universal-conormal] identifies the other two ideals with $\mathcal C_{Y/X}$ and $\mathcal C_{Z/X}$.

source.place: Tag 06BF, lemma-transitivity-conormal-unramified, part (1) and its universal-property argument; Tag 03MB in spaces-morphisms.tex for ideals and factorization.

proof.text: Right exactness, including the specified arrows. At a geometric point $\bar z$ write $A'=\mathcal O_{W_v,u\bar z}$, $B'=\mathcal O_{W_{vu},\bar z}$, $I=\mathcal I_{u\bar z}$, $K=\mathcal K_{\bar z}$, $A=A'/I$ and $B=B'/K$. By [lem-sfb-space-stalk-ideal-pullback], the stalk of $u^*\mathcal C_{Y/X}$ is $I\otimes_A B$ and $\lambda(i\otimes b)=h^\sharp(i)\widetilde b$, where $\widetilde b$ is any lift to $B'$. The same node identifies $\mathcal L_{\bar z}=IB'\subseteq K$. Since $K^2=0$, $K$ annihilates $h^\sharp(I)$, so the displayed map is well-defined and its image is exactly $IB'$. Step 2 and [lem-sfb-space-universal-conormal] identify the third stalk with $K/IB'$. The ideal map for $P\to W_{vu}$ gives $\rho(k)=k\bmod IB'$. Consequently $\rho$ is onto and $\ker\rho=IB'=\operatorname{im}\lambda$. The exact and conservative geometric stalks of [lem-sfb-space-stalk-ideal-pullback] give the asserted right exact sequence: stalks of its kernel modulo its image are zero, hence that module is zero. This uses no injectivity assertion for $\lambda$.

source.place: Tag 06BF, lemma-transitivity-conormal-unramified, part (2); the square-zero ideal calculation supplies the uses of Tags 06BD and 04CQ in its proof without importing their more general immersion statements.

proof.text: The lifting input for etale maps. A representable etale map $E\to H$ has a unique lift in every square-zero lifting problem with affine scheme tests $T\hookrightarrow T'$: by [def-trf-algebraic-space], $E\times_H T'$ is an etale scheme over $T'$, hence flat and unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-unramified-formally-etale] to this scheme map and the given section over $T$. For an arbitrary scheme $T'$, do this on affine opens (their inverse images in $T$ are affine by the affine-quotient characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion]); the unique lifts agree on affine covers of their intersections and glue. For algebraic-space tests, choose a surjective etale scheme atlas of $T'$ and pull it back to $T$ using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The scheme lifts agree on the scheme relation of the atlas, by uniqueness, and descend because $E$ is a sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Thus the same existence and uniqueness holds for algebraic-space tests. This is the representable case of formal etaleness; it uses no finiteness of the test spaces.

source.place: Tag 04AL, lemma-representable-property-formally-property, part (2), with the affine-test scheme lifting theorem; Tag 0604, lemma-universal-thickening-over-formally-etale, for the following application.

proof.text: Localize both source and target. In the square of the statement, two maps $T'\to V$ over $U$ agreeing on $T$ have equal composites into $B$ by formal unramifiedness of $B/A$, and are then equal by the uniqueness of the lift along $V\to B$ from step 4. This proves that $V/U$ is formally unramified; the same argument proves that $V/A$ is formally unramified. Apply [lem-sfb-space-universal-thickening-etale-transfer] to the etale map $V\to B$ and the universal thickening $B\hookrightarrow W_{B/A}$. It provides a universal thickening $V\hookrightarrow W$ over $A$, with $W\to W_{B/A}$ etale and $V=B\times_{W_{B/A}}W$. Step 4 applied to $U\to A$ gives a unique map $W\to U$ extending $V\to U$. Given a test thickening over $U$ mapping into $V$, extend uniquely to $W$ over $A$. Its composite into $U$ is the prescribed structural map, since both extend the same map on $T$ and $U\to A$ has unique lifting. Therefore $W$ is universal over $U$. The uniqueness of universal thickenings in [lem-sfb-space-universal-conormal] identifies $W$ with $W_{V/U}$ and its map with the canonical map of step 1. No cartesianness of the original square was used.

source.place: Tag 060D, lemma-universal-thickening-localize, using Tag 0605, lemma-etale-morphism-of-universal-thickenings, part (1), and the lifting argument of Tag 0604.

proof.text: The conormal identification and the stated special case. The square $V\hookrightarrow W$ over $B\hookrightarrow W_{B/A}$ in step 5 is cartesian with etale ambient map. By [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence], its ideal is precisely the etale restriction of the ideal of $B$, and [lem-sfb-space-universal-conormal] identifies these square-zero ideals with the two conormal modules. The ideal map is the restriction isomorphism itself: it sends a restricted section $i$ to that same section. Tensor pullback along the etale map agrees with restriction by [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction]. This proves the claimed identification for the induced map. If $D\to W_{B/A}$ is etale, put $B_D=B\times_{W_{B/A}}D$. Its map to $B$ is etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Now $(B_D\hookrightarrow D)\to(B\hookrightarrow W_{B/A})$ is an etale cartesian map of first-order thickenings. Part (1) of [lem-sfb-space-universal-thickening-etale-transfer], and its uniqueness of the etale thickening extending $B_D\to B$, identify $D$ with the universal thickening of $B_D$ over $A$.

source.place: Tags 060D and 0605, lemma-universal-thickening-localize and lemma-etale-morphism-of-universal-thickenings (1); Tag 03MB in spaces-morphisms.tex for etale restriction of the closed-subspace ideal.

proof.text: Compatibility with squares and tower charts. The construction in step 1 commutes with composition by uniqueness. For compatible etale charts $Z_0\to Y_0\to X_0$ of $Z\to Y\to X$, the maps of the universal thickenings over $X_0$ and $X$ therefore commute with $h$. The induced map $Y_0\times_{W_{Y_0/X_0}}W_{Z_0/X_0}\to Y\times_{W_v}W_{vu}$ commutes with their inclusions into the ambient universal thickenings, by the fibre-product equations. For $\lambda$, pulling an ideal section along either path gives the same section, and on tensors the value is in both cases $h^\sharp(i)\widetilde b$. For $\rho$, both paths send $k$ to its image modulo the pulled-back ideal $\mathcal L$. These are the canonical ideal-map formulas of [lem-sfb-space-stalk-ideal-pullback]; equality may be checked on its conservative stalks. Step 6 identifies the vertical ideal maps with the restriction isomorphisms. To identify the tensor-pullback sources, [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] supplies composition of the ringed morphisms; the tensor definition [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] identifies the two pullbacks by multiplication of scalar coefficients. The equality follows from the commuting square of ring maps, including for squares that are not cartesian. Hence the restriction isomorphisms identify both $\lambda$ and $\rho$ with their chart versions. Nothing requires a nonidentity change on $X$; taking $X_0=X$ gives the asserted identity-base charts.
